newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion fraud suit against ABC-TV opens.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion fraud suit against ABC-TV opens.

text.p: Food Lion Inc's lawsuit against the ABC television network began today with Food Lion accusing the network of fraud by having its producers work undercover as store employees in order to obtain a story.
Food Lion lead attorney Andrew Copenhaver said ABC had practiced deception against the grocery chain when it let two of its producers apply for jobs at the grocery store.
"They will admit that at no time did they tell Food Lion about their employment with ABC," he said.
He said once the producers were hired they did not act as Food Lion employees, but worked for ABC, by going into Food Lion stores equipped with spying equipment.
ABC attorney Bill Jeffress denied two producers had committed fraud in gathering information for a program that claimed grocer Food Lion Inc sold old food.
But Jeffress said that ABC would not contest the allegation that there was deception in the case.
"There is no question there was deception. There was not fraud," he said.
The trial comes four years after ABC's newsmagazine "PrimeTime Live" aired the report which said that Food Lion workers sold out-of-date merchandise and changed expiration dates on other items.

Salisbury, N.C.-based Food Lion, a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA, is charging fraud, deceptive trade practices, conspiracy and breach of duty of loyalty against ABC and its producers.
Food Lion claims its workers were coerced by the ABC producers working undercover with hidden cameras at two of its stores.
The producers were in the Food Lion stores for about three weeks. They took 34 hidden camera tapes, which amounted to 45 hours.
"We believe the evidence of the footage will show you they weren't acting as Food Lion employees," Copenhaver said.
Jeffress said the two producers wore small cameras in wigs and recorders under their smocks, and were told by their supervisors to ask as many questions as they needed to while working at Food Lion.
"What's at issue in the case is whether they did the job they were hired to do," Jeffress said.
"The evidence will satisfy you that they did do their job, they faked nothing, they committed no fraud, no trespass, no breach of duty," he added.
